name: Meropenem
executiveSummary: Broad-spectrum carbapenem. Adult 1 g IV every 8 h (meningitis/CF 2 g every 8 h). Pediatrics 20 mg/kg every 8 h (60 mg/kg/day); CNS/sepsis 40 mg/kg every 8 h (120 mg/kg/day; max 6 g/day).
indications:
## Indications

- Severe infections due to MDR gram-negatives, anaerobes, and many gram-positives (not MRSA/E. faecium).
- Bacterial meningitis, sepsis, CF, complicated intra-abdominal infections when spectrum justifies.

## Precautions

- Adjust in renal failure. Seizures (lower risk than imipenem, still possible in CNS/renal failure).
- Resistance selection — reserve use.

> Prolonged infusion (3 h) may be used in critical care per PK/PD protocol.

adulto.dose: Usual severe infections: **1 g IV every 8 h**. Meningitis / CF / very severe: **2 g every 8 h**. Mandatory renal adjustment.
adulto.administration: IV push: reconstitute in sterile water; 5 min. Intermittent IV: dilute in 50–100 mL NS/5% dextrose; 15–30 min (or 3 h if extended-infusion protocol).
adulto.notes: Fluid restriction: may concentrate per label.

pediatrico.dose: UTI/skin/other: **20 mg/kg every 8 h** (**60 mg/kg/day**; max **3 g/day**). Sepsis/CNS/CF: **40 mg/kg every 8 h** (**120 mg/kg/day**; max **6 g/day**).
pediatrico.notes: Dose by weight. > 50 kg: adult dose.

neonatal.dose: Orientative: **20 mg/kg/dose every 12–24 h** in preterms by PMA/PNA; meningitis may need 40 mg/kg — follow NNU table.
neonatal.notes: Always cross-check the center neonatal protocol.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: use promptly (short room-temp stability).
- Diluted in NS is usually more stable than in dextrose — check label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Diarrhea, nausea, rash, phlebitis, ↑ transaminases, thrombocytosis/thrombocytopenia, seizures (rare), *C. difficile*.
